From 9862ef9ab0a116c6dca98842aab7de13a252ae02 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:39:24 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: ipset: drop logically empty buckets in mtype_del

mtype_del() counts empty slots below n->pos in k, but it only drops the
bucket when both n->pos and k are zero. This misses buckets whose live
entries have all been removed while n->pos still points past deleted slots.

Treat a bucket as empty when all positions below n->pos are unused and
release it directly instead of shrinking it further.

Fixes: 8af1c6fbd923 ("netfilter: ipset: Fix forceadd evaluation path")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Xin Liu <dstsmallbird@foxmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Co-developed-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Phil Sutter <phil@nwl.cc>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_hash_gen.h b/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_hash_gen.h
index 181daa9c2019..b79e5dd2af03 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_hash_gen.h
+++ b/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_hash_gen.h
@@ -1098,7 +1098,7 @@ mtype_del(struct ip_set *set, void *value, const struct ip_set_ext *ext,
 			if (!test_bit(i, n->used))
 				k++;
 		}
-		if (n->pos == 0 && k == 0) {
+		if (k == n->pos) {
 			t->hregion[r].ext_size -= ext_size(n->size, dsize);
 			rcu_assign_pointer(hbucket(t, key), NULL);
 			kfree_rcu(n, rcu);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch addresses a bug in the `netfilter/ipset` subsystem where logically empty hash buckets were not being freed during element deletion (`mtype_del`). The fix modifies the condition that determines whether a bucket should be released.

## Modifications

### File: `net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_hash_gen.h`

**Changed condition (line 1098):**  
- **Before:** `if (n->pos == 0 && k == 0)`  
- **After:** `if (k == n->pos)`

### Relationship

- The original condition required both `n->pos` (the highest occupied position index) to be zero and `k` (the count of empty slots below `n->pos`) to be zero. This only recognized a bucket as empty when no entries had ever been placed beyond index 0 and all slots were unused.
- The bug occurred when all live entries in a bucket were removed, but `n->pos` still pointed to a position beyond the last removed entry (e.g., after earlier deletions). In such cases, `n->pos` could be >0 while all entries below it were empty (i.e., `k == n->pos`). The old condition failed to detect this, so the bucket remained allocated with dead space.
- The new condition correctly identifies a bucket as empty when **all** positions below `n->pos` are unused (`k` equals `n->pos`). This ensures that a bucket whose last live entries have been removed is freed immediately rather than being retained unnecessarily, preventing resource waste and potential inconsistency.

Here is the commit message:
netfilter: ipset: drop logically empty buckets in mtype_del

mtype_del() counts empty slots below n->pos in k, but it only drops the
bucket when both n->pos and k are zero. This misses buckets whose live
entries have all been removed while n->pos still points past deleted slots.

Treat a bucket as empty when all positions below n->pos are unused and
release it directly instead of shrinking it further.

Fixes: 8af1c6fbd923 ("netfilter: ipset: Fix forceadd evaluation path")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Xin Liu <dstsmallbird@foxmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>

Reviewed-by: Phil Sutter <phil@nwl.cc>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect condition in the `mtype_del()` function for determining when a hash bucket should be freed. The original condition `if (n->pos == 0 && k == 0)` only freed a bucket when its highest occupied position index (`n->pos`) was zero *and* the count of empty slots below it (`k`) was zero. This missed cases where all live entries in a bucket had been removed, but `n->pos` still pointed to a position beyond the deleted slots (i.e., `k == n->pos` but `n->pos > 0`). As a result, such logically empty buckets were retained indefinitely, wasting memory and potentially causing inconsistencies during forced additions or lookups.
